Meta Test Description: The testcase performs PCIe device enumeration across two dual-mode controllers (DM0 and DM1). It begins by writing 0x0 to 0xE6004100 to initialize the system. It then invokes link training (link_training_dm0_x4 or link_training_dm1_x4) based on compile-time defines (DM0_RC, DM1_RC, DM0_EP, DM1_EP). Cache coherency programming is performed by reading mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF and mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF, modifying specific bit fields using set_data at bit positions [11:14], [3:6], [27:30], and [19:22] with value 0xf, and writing back. A wait_on(20) delay is inserted between coherency programming phases. The test then polls read_sii0_reg(0xC0) in a while loop until (data_rd & 0xD1) == 0xD1, and similarly polls read_sii1_reg(0xC0) for the same link-up condition. Under DM0_RC, the Vendor ID is read from read_pcie_slv0_reg(0x0), the command register is written via write_pcie_slv0_reg(0x4, 0x7) to enable IO, Memory, and Bus Master, and memory base programming functions mem_base_program_dm0_x4 and mem_base_program_dm1_x4 are called. System-level registers at 0xE690000C, 0xE6900010, 0xE6900014, 0xE6900018, 0xE6900030, and 0xE6900034 are written with 0x1. Cache coherency is then disabled by writing 0x0 to bit fields [19:22] and [27:30] of both COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF registers. After a wait_on(30), BAR sizing is performed on the endpoint via write_pcie_slv1_reg and read_pcie_slv1_reg for offsets 0x10, 0x14, 0x18, 0x1c, 0x20, 0x24 by writing 0xFFFFFFFF, reading back, then writing actual base addresses. The same BAR sizing sequence is repeated for slv0. Finally, the test polls 0xE6004100 in a while loop until the value equals 0x12345678, then calls finish(0).

Meta Test Description: The testcase performs PCIe DMA write and read operations across four channels on either DM0 or DM1 controller based on compile-time defines. It begins by writing 0x0 to 0xE6004100 to initialize the system. Link training is invoked via link_training_dm0_x4(4) or link_training_dm1_x4(4) depending on DM0_RC, DM1_RC, DM0_EP, or DM1_EP defines. Under DM0_RC, the SII0 link status is polled via read_sii0_reg(0xC0) in a while loop until (data_rd & 0xD1) == 0xD1. The Vendor ID is read via read_pcie_slv0_reg(0x0), the command register is written via write_pcie_slv0_reg(0x4, 0x7) to enable IO, Memory, and Bus Master, and bar_program_dm0_x4() and mem_base_program_dm0_x4() are called. Under DM1_RC, the same sequence is performed using SII1 and slv1 interfaces. The test then polls 0xE6004100 in a while loop until the value equals 0x12345678 with wait_on(5) between iterations. Source memory at src_addr0 (0xE6000000) is preloaded with 128 words of 0xC0DEBEED and 128 words of 0xF00DDEAF. GIC interrupts are configured via GIC_Set() and GIC_EnableAllIRQ(), and int_pend is set to 1. Under DM0_RC, DMA interrupt masks are cleared by writing 0x0 to mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF and mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF. DMA write channels 0-3 are programmed via program_dma_wch0 through program_dma_wch3 with source, destination, and length parameters, and each channel is triggered by writing the channel number (0x0-0x3) to mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF. After each doorbell write, the test waits in a while(int_pend) loop with wait_on(10) for the interrupt handler to clear int_pend, then resets int_pend to 1. DMA read channels 0-3 are similarly programmed via program_dma_rch0 through program_dma_rch3 and triggered by writing channel numbers to mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF. Under DM1_RC, the same DMA write and read sequence is performed using mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF, mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF, mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF, and mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF. The Default_IRQHandler reads mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF and mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF (or PCIE1 equivalents under DM1_RC), masks the lower 4 bits with 0x0000000F, clears interrupts by writing the status to mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF and mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF (or PCIE1 equivalents), sets int_pend to 0, and calls GIC_ClearIRQ(0x20) for DM0 or GIC_ClearIRQ(0x23) for DM1. The test ends with finish(0).
